Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

sunshine noun

also sun

classical

sōl, sōlis m.

noun, third declension

Ordinary physical sense.

Examples

  • «Nunc quidem paululum,» inquit, «ā sōle.» Offēcerat vidēlicet aprīcantī.

    “Just now,” he said, “a little out of my sun.” Alexander, you see, was standing in his light as he basked (Diogenes, when Alexander asked if he needed anything).Cic. Tusc. 5.92

Other words

  • 1aprīcor: short a (Lewis & Short ā̆prīcor, common). Hor. C. 1.8.3, perdere, cūr aprīcum, an Aristophanic (— ∪ ∪ — ∪ — —): a- takes the short place. De Vaan 47 marks only the ī of aprīcus.

    aprīcor1, aprīcārī — sit in the sun, bask

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 5.92; Col. 8.4.6 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 387

    To sun oneself; Traupman’s word for sunbathing.

See also shade, sun.
